audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Job's continued discourse: oath by the living Divine, refusal to surrender integrity, rejection of false speech, and description of the godless person's fragile hope and wealth. Preserves tension: Job rejects friends' accusations while still affirming that godlessness has no final security.

verses.restored: Job again took up his discourse and said:

familiar.text: Moreover Job continued his parable, and said,

modern.text: Job continued his discourse:

original.text: וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר

verses.restored: As the Divine lives, who has removed my justice, and Shaddai, who has made my soul bitter,

familiar.text: As God liveth, who hath taken away my judgment; and the Almighty, who hath vexed my soul;

modern.text: “As surely as God lives, who has deprived me of justice— the Almighty, who has embittered my soul—

original.text: חַי אֵ֭ל הֵסִ֣יר מִשְׁפָּטִ֑י וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י הֵמַ֥ר נַפְשִֽׁי

verses.restored: as long as my breath is still in me, and the breath of the Divine is in my nostrils,

familiar.text: All the while my breath is in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils;

modern.text: as long as my breath is still within me and the breath of God remains in my nostrils,

original.text: כִּֽי כָל ע֣וֹד נִשְׁמָתִ֣י בִ֑י וְר֖וּחַ אֱל֣וֹהַּ בְּאַפִּֽי

verses.restored: my lips will not speak injustice, and my tongue will not utter deceit.

familiar.text: My lips shall not speak wickedness, nor my tongue utter deceit.

modern.text: my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.

original.text: אִם תְּדַבֵּ֣רְנָה שְׂפָתַ֣י עַוְלָ֑ה וּ֝לְשׁוֹנִ֗י אִם יֶהְגֶּ֥ה רְמִיָּֽה

verses.restored: Far be it from me to say you are right; until I expire, I will not remove my integrity from me.

familiar.text: God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.

modern.text: I will never say that you are right; I will maintain my integrity until I die.

original.text: חָלִ֣ילָה לִּי֮ אִם אַצְדִּ֪יק אֶ֫תְכֶ֥ם עַד אֶגְוָ֑ע לֹא אָסִ֖יר תֻּמָּתִ֣י מִמֶּֽנִּי

verses.restored: I hold fast my righteousness and will not let it go; my heart does not reproach any of my days.

familiar.text: My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: my heart shall not reproach me so long as I live.

modern.text: I will cling to my righteousness and never let go. As long as I live, my conscience will not accuse me. The Wicked Man’s Portion

original.text: בְּצִדְקָתִ֣י הֶ֭חֱזַקְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אַרְפֶּ֑הָ לֹֽא יֶחֱרַ֥ף לְ֝בָבִ֗י מִיָּמָֽי

verses.restored: Let my enemy be as the wicked, and the one rising against me as the unjust.

familiar.text: Let mine enemy be as the wicked, and he that riseth up against me as the unrighteous.

modern.text: May my enemy be like the wicked and my opponent like the unjust.

original.text: יְהִ֣י כְ֭רָשָׁע אֹ֣יְבִ֑י וּמִתְקוֹמְמִ֥י כְעַוָּֽל

verses.restored: For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when the Divine draws out his soul?

familiar.text: For what is the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when God taketh away his soul?

modern.text: For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?

original.text: כִּ֤י מַה תִּקְוַ֣ת חָ֭נֵף כִּ֣י יִבְצָ֑ע כִּ֤י יֵ֖שֶׁל אֱל֣וֹהַּ נַפְשֽׁוֹ

verses.restored: Will the Divine hear his cry when distress comes upon him?

familiar.text: Will God hear his cry when trouble cometh upon him?

modern.text: Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?

original.text: הַֽ֭צַעֲקָתוֹ יִשְׁמַ֥ע אֵ֑ל כִּֽי תָב֖וֹא עָלָ֣יו צָרָֽה

verses.restored: Will he delight himself in Shaddai? Will he call upon the Divine at all times?

familiar.text: Will he delight himself in the Almighty? will he always call upon God?

modern.text: Will he delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?

original.text: אִם עַל שַׁדַּ֥י יִתְעַנָּ֑ג יִקְרָ֖א אֱל֣וֹהַּ בְּכָל עֵֽת

verses.restored: I will teach you about the hand of the Divine; what is with Shaddai I will not hide.

familiar.text: I will teach you by the hand of God: that which is with the Almighty will I not conceal.

modern.text: I will instruct you in the power of God. I will not conceal the ways of the Almighty.

original.text: אוֹרֶ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֣ם בְּיַד אֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִם שַׁ֝דַּ֗י לֹ֣א אֲכַחֵֽד

verses.restored: Look, all of you have seen it; why then have you become altogether empty?

familiar.text: Behold, all ye yourselves have seen it; why then are ye thus altogether vain?

modern.text: Surely all of you have seen it for yourselves. Why then do you keep up this empty talk?

original.text: הֵן אַתֶּ֣ם כֻּלְּכֶ֣ם חֲזִיתֶ֑ם וְלָמָּה זֶּ֝֗ה הֶ֣בֶל תֶּהְבָּֽלוּ

verses.restored: This is the portion of a wicked person with the Divine, and the inheritance ruthless ones receive from Shaddai:

familiar.text: This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage of oppressors, which they shall receive of the Almighty.

modern.text: This is the wicked man’s portion from God— the heritage the ruthless receive from the Almighty.

original.text: זֶ֤ה חֵֽלֶק אָדָ֖ם רָשָׁ֥ע עִם אֵ֑ל וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת עָ֝רִיצִ֗ים מִשַּׁדַּ֥י יִקָּֽחוּ

verses.restored: If his children multiply, it is for the sword, and his offspring will not be satisfied with bread.

familiar.text: If his children be multiplied, it is for the sword: and his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.

modern.text: Though his sons are many, they are destined for the sword; and his offspring will never have enough food.

original.text: אִם יִרְבּ֣וּ בָנָ֣יו לְמוֹ חָ֑רֶב וְ֝צֶאֱצָאָ֗יו לֹ֣א יִשְׂבְּעוּ לָֽחֶם

verses.restored: Those who remain of him will be buried by death, and his widows will not weep.

familiar.text: Those that remain of him shall be buried in death: and his widows shall not weep.

modern.text: His survivors will be buried by the plague, and their widows will not weep for them.

original.text: שרידו בַּמָּ֣וֶת יִקָּבֵ֑רוּ וְ֝אַלְמְנֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִבְכֶּֽינָה

verses.restored: Though he piles up silver like dust and prepares clothing like clay,

familiar.text: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare raiment as the clay;

modern.text: Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up a wardrobe like clay,

original.text: אִם יִצְבֹּ֣ר כֶּעָפָ֣ר כָּ֑סֶף וְ֝כַחֹ֗מֶר יָכִ֥ין מַלְבּֽוּשׁ

verses.restored: he prepares it, but the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide the silver.

familiar.text: He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.

modern.text: what he lays up, the righteous will wear, and his silver will be divided by the innocent.

original.text: יָ֭כִין וְצַדִּ֣יק יִלְבָּ֑שׁ וְ֝כֶ֗סֶף נָקִ֥י יַחֲלֹֽק

verses.restored: He builds his house like a moth, like a booth a watchman makes.

familiar.text: He buildeth his house as a moth, and as a booth that the keeper maketh.

modern.text: The house he built is like a moth’s cocoon, like a hut set up by a watchman.

original.text: בָּנָ֣ה כָעָ֣שׁ בֵּית֑וֹ וּ֝כְסֻכָּ֗ה עָשָׂ֥ה נֹצֵֽר

verses.restored: Rich he lies down, but it will not be gathered; he opens his eyes, and it is not there.

familiar.text: The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered: he openeth his eyes, and he is not.

modern.text: He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone.

original.text: עָשִׁ֣יר יִ֭שְׁכַּב וְלֹ֣א יֵאָסֵ֑ף עֵינָ֖יו פָּקַ֣ח וְאֵינֶֽנּוּ

verses.restored: Terrors overtake him like waters; a storm steals him away in the night.

familiar.text: Terrors take hold on him as waters, a tempest stealeth him away in the night.

modern.text: Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest sweeps him away in the night.

original.text: תַּשִּׂיגֵ֣הוּ כַ֭מַּיִם בַּלָּה֑וֹת לַ֝֗יְלָה גְּנָבַ֥תּוּ סוּפָֽה

verses.restored: The east wind lifts him, and he goes; it sweeps him from his place.

familiar.text: The east wind carrieth him away, and he departeth: and as a storm hurleth him out of his place.

modern.text: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.

original.text: יִשָּׂאֵ֣הוּ קָדִ֣ים וְיֵלַ֑ךְ וִֽ֝ישָׂעֲרֵ֗הוּ מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ

familiar.text: For God shall cast upon him, and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand.

modern.text: It hurls itself against him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power.

original.text: וְיַשְׁלֵ֣ךְ עָ֭לָיו וְלֹ֣א יַחְמֹ֑ל מִ֝יָּד֗וֹ בָּר֥וֹחַ יִבְרָֽח

verses.restored: It claps its hands over him and hisses him from his place.

familiar.text: Men shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.

modern.text: It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place.
